meta.title: Questions that need answering before a decision can be made
meta.rule: Each question states what we know, what we do not know, why the answer changes a decision, and the cheapest concrete step that would produce the answer. A question with no such step is not a question, it is a wish — none of those are listed.

priority_key.P1: Blocks a decision that is being made now
priority_key.P2: Blocks a decision in the next build
priority_key.P3: Worth knowing, no decision depends on it yet

rows.question: Is this project trying to beat a market, or to measure model quality?
rows.known: No licensed odds feed is connected and no NBA-operated price exists. Every edge on the site is model-vs-naive-model at a -110 convention chosen by the repository.
rows.missing: A decision, plus — if the answer is 'beat a market' — a dated, licensed closing-price source per game.
rows.why_it_decides: It changes what 'validated' means. Against a market, S1 must beat a real price and pay real vig. Against a naive model, S1 is already mildly ahead on margin (MAE 12.98 vs 13.62) and behind on totals (14.83 vs 14.72).
rows.how_to_discover: Either (a) buy a licensed historical + closing-line feed and backfill the 60-game window, or (b) publish one sentence on the landing page: 'this project measures model quality; no market edge is claimed or measurable'. Option (b) costs nothing and can be done today.
rows.blocks: Gate G7, the leaderboard's meaning, and every 'edge' label on the site

rows.question: Do NBA.com's terms permit publishing derived lines and a paid reward structure?
rows.known: The site publishes derived numbers built on official data, and the brief describes rewards for top strategies.
rows.missing: A reading of NBA.com's terms of use for derived commercial content. This session can read the page but cannot give a legal opinion, and nothing in the repository states the terms under which the data is used.
rows.why_it_decides: If derived commercial use is not permitted, the reward/leaderboard framing has to change before it is built, not after.
rows.how_to_discover: Read https://www.nba.com/termsofuse and, if the reward structure is real money, take one hour of legal advice. Record the conclusion in the repository so the next session does not re-litigate it.
rows.blocks: Any monetised leaderboard, and the site's public framing

rows.question: Is S1 real, or is it the best of six lottery tickets?
rows.known: 23-9, p = 0.020 against a coin flip, Wilson lower bound 0.546. It fails calibration and stability.
rows.missing: A corrected significance figure and a pre-registered replication. BH across the six tested strategies gives q = 0.120, and S1's win rate barely changes with edge size (r = 0.051).
rows.why_it_decides: It is the difference between 'one strategy shows a signal worth funding at quarter size' and 'nothing has demonstrated skill yet'.
rows.how_to_discover: Pre-register S1 exactly as it stands, then grade the next 60 games with no changes. At 32 games the design can only detect a very large edge; about 250-300 graded picks are needed to separate 55% from 52.4% at 80% power.

rows.question: What is the true injury-driven minutes and production impact, and how do we keep it current?
rows.known: The injury layer exists and is rule-based, but it is built on the 04:15 AM edition on a game day. Twenty-two designations changed by 1:30 PM. Minutes are known for only 24 players in the repository.
rows.missing: A per-team minutes distribution (all rotation players, not the top 24 league-wide), and an ingestion path that picks up the latest edition instead of a hand-captured one.
rows.why_it_decides: The brief asks specifically for injury-driven rotation and production analysis. Right now the impact number is a lower bound computed over a small slice of players, on a stale report.
rows.how_to_discover: Pull each team's official roster minutes from the Players Traditional table filtered by team (30 requests, all official), then re-price every game against the latest edition and compare before/after.
rows.blocks: The props layer and any availability-based strategy (S6, S7, S8)

rows.question: Does '3 days in advance' mean today+3 calendar dates, or a 72-hour window?
rows.known: The build publishes 11/14 through 11/17 — 27 games, four calendar dates.
rows.missing: A stated rule. The two readings differ by one slate (five games on 11/17).
rows.why_it_decides: The 11/17 games have no injury report at all (all 28 team-slots NOT YET SUBMITTED), so they are the lowest-information picks on the page. Whether they belong in the horizon is a product decision, not a technical one.
rows.how_to_discover: State the rule on the picks page in one sentence and in the builder's header. No data collection needed.
rows.blocks: Horizon scope and the pick count headline

rows.question: Which of the six published builds is the product?
rows.known: Root site/ (Build D), command-center/, edge-lab/, docs/, docs/b/, origination/, plus five desk pages — all live, all linked from a switcher.
rows.missing: A designation of one current build, and a decision about whether the others are archive.
rows.why_it_decides: Every improvement spends effort on one of six codebases. Fixing S1's statistics in one build leaves five other pages saying something different.
rows.how_to_discover: Pick the build whose pipeline the next session should extend (the root site is the only one that rebuilds idempotently and passes its own gate), and move the rest under a single /archive/ path with a banner. No data work needed.
rows.blocks: All engineering suggestions S-01 to S-06

rows.question: For player props, what exactly is the 'line' being bet against?
rows.known: Prop lines are the players' official season averages, sometimes one game stale, and the model's projection is that average adjusted for pace and opponent.
rows.missing: A stated definition. A season average is not a market line: it has no juice, no half-point, and no closing value.
rows.why_it_decides: With an average as the line, an 'over' pick is close to a coin flip by construction unless the adjustment is genuinely predictive. That is why S7 and S8 have zero graded plays.
rows.how_to_discover: Either define a fixed convention (e.g. 'line = season average rounded to 0.5, graded at even money') and publish it, or drop prop picks until a real line source exists.
rows.blocks: Player props, prop combos, same-game parlays

rows.question: How should correlated legs be priced across a parlay?
rows.known: Thirteen correlations among official team stats are measured and reproduce exactly. The same-game-parlay rho values are model guesses (0.0, 0.25, 0.30, -0.20, 0.05) and the site labels them as guesses.
rows.missing: A measured rho for any parlay pair that involves a player, which needs a player game-log corpus. The repository holds game logs for 3 players.
rows.why_it_decides: Parlay pricing is the whole of the brief's 'parlay and prop combo' section. With guessed rho, a parlay price is a guess with extra steps.
rows.how_to_discover: Collect official player game logs for the 60-game window (one request per player per season via the official stats pages), then measure pairwise rho directly instead of assuming it.

rows.question: Is the rest signal real, and can we trust the field that carries it?
rows.known: The repository reports a rest-day differential worth about +2.82 points per game at p = 0.130, needing roughly 340 games. The field itself is currently computed wrongly in the horizon build (26 of 27 rows negative).
rows.missing: A correct rest table across the season, and enough games to detect an effect that small.
rows.why_it_decides: Rest is one of the few signals that is not just a re-expression of team quality, so it is worth getting right — but only after the field is correct.
rows.how_to_discover: Fix the rest computation (F-12), widen the corpus to the full season from the official schedule, then re-estimate.
rows.blocks: Rest/back-to-back strategies (S5 is already 8-4 on this basis and unvalidated)

rows.question: Which official injury designations actually move a line?
rows.known: Statuses are mapped to weights (Out 1.0, Doubtful, Questionable 0.35, Probable, Available) and to a 15 net-rating-points-per-100-possessions impact if a full team of minutes were lost.
rows.missing: Any measured relationship between a designation and the player's actual minutes. The weights are asserted, not fitted.
rows.why_it_decides: If 'Questionable' means a 70% chance of playing 34 minutes, weighting it at 0.35 mis-prices the game. Nothing in the repository tests this.
rows.how_to_discover: Join the official injury reports (every edition for a fortnight) to the box scores of those games and measure realised minutes by designation. That is a self-contained, entirely official dataset.

rows.question: How much of the model's error is pace, and how much is efficiency?
rows.known: Totals are the weak spot: model MAE 14.83 vs naive 14.72, while margin MAE is 12.98 vs 13.62. The model uses PACE and OffRtg/DefRtg scaled by league averages.
rows.missing: An error decomposition. No page separates 'we got the pace wrong' from 'we got the shooting wrong'.
rows.why_it_decides: It tells the next build whether to spend effort on pace modelling or on efficiency modelling — a fork in the road with very different data requirements.
rows.how_to_discover: Regress total error on predicted pace and predicted offensive rating across the 60 games. Both series already exist in the repository.

rows.question: What does a 'reward' for a top strategy actually consist of?
rows.known: The brief describes a leaderboard competition with rewards. The repository publishes reward tiers and caps (a quarter unit for an unvalidated strategy).
rows.missing: Whether rewards are money, ranking only, or nothing, and who funds them.
rows.why_it_decides: If money, every statistical claim becomes a conduct question (and Q-02 becomes urgent). If ranking only, the leaderboard is a research artefact and can be simpler.
rows.how_to_discover: Decide and write it down. No data needed.
